guide.summary: Dropbox documents per-user OAuth 2.0 for apps acting on a user's data. Listing names and metadata in an App Folder requires the files.metadata.read scope, and list_folder/continue supports pagination until has_more is false. App registration, redirect setup and the OAuth flow are untested. Distribution rules for other customer organizations are not in the supplied snapshots.
guide.recommendation: The requested access is documented. Follow the saved setup steps and run each representative API test; execution has not been verified.

findings.title: Per-user OAuth 2.0 access token for each connected account
findings.detail: Dropbox uses OAuth 2.0 so the app accesses data on behalf of each user. Apps requesting only User API scopes receive a token associated with the user who authorizes the app, which fits per-account access without team administration.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer authorizes the app with their own Dropbox account and no team administration is requested

evidence.quote: Apps that request only scopes from the User API will receive a token associated with the user that authorizes the app.
Dropbox uses OAuth 2.0
be used by your app in subsequent API calls for that user. It should be passed with the Authorization HTTP header value of Bearer <oauth2-access-token>

steps.detail: Build the authorization URL with client_id, redirect_uri and response_type=code, and send the customer to it. The customer approves the app for their own account. The callback must return an authorization code and a matching state value.

steps.doneWhen: Token endpoint returns an access_token and expires_in, and the token is stored only for that customer account.

steps.title: List first page of App Folder entries
steps.detail: Call list_folder with path set to the empty string to list the App Folder root. Do not send a limit parameter; it is not documented for this operation. Each item in the entries array carries metadata such as name, and its .tag value distinguishes file from folder. The top-level cursor and has_more fields control pagination.
steps.doneWhen: Response is 200 with an entries array, a cursor string, and a has_more boolean. Entries contain metadata only, such as name and .tag. Boundary check: confirm the granted scope is files.metadata.read and the outgoing request log shows only list_folder and list_folder/continue calls, with no content download or write endpoints.

evidence.quote: Required scope: files.metadata.read Endpoint format: RPC
--data ' {"path": ""} '
entries list of objects

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN: OAuth access token for the individual test account from the exchange-code step
path: empty string for the App Folder root

steps.title: Continue listing until has_more is false
steps.detail: While has_more is true, call list_folder/continue with the cursor from the most recent response, replacing it with each newly returned cursor. Add each page's entries to one collected list of names and metadata. Stop only when has_more is false. A page with no entries does not end the listing by itself.
steps.doneWhen: The loop ends on a response with has_more set to false, after all pages are collected. Boundary check: confirm the granted scope is files.metadata.read and the request log contains only list_folder/continue calls after the first page, with no download or write endpoints.
